info.name: PixelGrade AI — API
info.description:
PixelGrade AI backend — organized by FRONTEND SCREEN, so the folder for the page you are building contains every request that page needs.

## Quick start

1. `npm run dev:local`
2. Run **00 · Auth › Login** — tokens are captured automatically into collection variables; every request inherits `Bearer {{accessToken}}`.
3. Open the folder matching your screen and go top to bottom.

A request used by two screens appears in both folders on purpose — each folder is self-sufficient.

## Chained variables

Creating things writes ids back automatically: Login → accessToken/refreshToken/userId · List plans → planId · Search catalogue → cardId · Create analysis → analysisId · Grade → reportId · Create slab → slabLabelId · Create ticket → ticketId.

## The one flow that must run in order

**01 · User Dashboard › New Analysis (Scan)** — upload → create → CONFIRM (hard server gate) → grade. Grading returns 400 until confirm has run.

## Admin folders

Log in as admin/super_admin first; a `user` token gets 403.

item.name: 00 · Auth & Onboarding
item.description:
Frontend pages: /signup, /verify-code, /login, /forgot-password, /reset-password.

The signup flow is: Register → Send OTP → Verify OTP (marks the email verified) → Login. Login fails with 403 until the email is verified.

**Run Login before anything else** — it captures accessToken/refreshToken into collection variables automatically, and every other folder inherits them.

request.description: Password requires 8+ characters with an uppercase letter, a digit, and a special character. Phone is optional and must be E.164.
Rate limited to 5 per hour. Codes live in Redis with a 5–10 minute TTL.
`otp` must be exactly 6 digits.

// Clear stale tokens so a failed login cannot leave a previous

request.description:
Rate limited to 20 requests per 15 minutes.

Fails with 403 if the account's email is not verified, is blocked, or was soft-deleted.

Reads `refreshToken` from the cookie, NOT the body. Returns **201**, not 200.

If this 400s with "No refresh token received from cookies", log in again — Postman needs the cookie from a prior login against the same host.
Emails a reset link. The link carries the reset token that `reset-password` requires.

item.name: 01 · User Dashboard
item.description: Everything under /user-dashboard, one sub-folder per screen. Each folder is self-sufficient: it contains every request its screen needs, even when that request also appears elsewhere.

item.name: Dashboard Home
item.description:
Page: /user-dashboard

Stat cards row → My dashboard stats.
Collection value chart → Value over time.
Collection by set donut + value bars → By set.
Recent scans list → Recent reports.

request.description:
Five stat cards: `collectionValue`, `cardsInCollection`, `slabsOrdered`, `totalScans`, `averageGrade`.

Each is `{ value, delta }`. **`delta` is null when last month was zero** — render no chip rather than a fabricated +100%. `averageGrade` is null outright when nothing is graded.

One point per calendar month, oldest-first, as `{ month: "2026-07", value }`.

Two documented approximations: today's quantity is applied to every past month, and prices before a card's history begins are carried backwards from its earliest known quote.

item.name: New Analysis (Scan)
item.description:
Page: /user-dashboard/new-analysis

**This is the core product flow — run in order.**

```
Credit balance   → the credit card widget (10 credits = 1 scan)
1. Upload        → Quick import / PixelScope grids
2. Create        → debits credits, identifies via Scrydex (or the dev mock — see below)
   (search + get candidates → the confirm screen the frontend still needs)
3. Confirm       → HARD GATE, grading refuses until this runs
4. Grade         → the report
```

⚠️ The frontend has no card-confirmation screen yet, but step 3 is a hard server gate. `matchScore` on candidates is Scrydex's raw scale (~0.7–1.3+), NOT a percentage — never render it as "N% match".

🧪 DEV MODE: with MOCK_SCRYDEX=true (development only), identification returns three fixed mock candidates (Charizard/Pikachu/Blastoise, ids prefixed mock-) so this whole folder runs end-to-end WITHOUT Scrydex credentials. Pricing is mocked too, so the Price Tracker folder has moving data.

request.description: Returns the balance, `creditsPerScan` (10), and scans remaining.
Copy the returned `url` values into the next request's `images` array.

exec: pm.expect(pm.response.code, 'a 402 means the balance is under 10 credits').to.not.equal(402);

request.description:
**Costs 10 credits.** A shortfall returns **402 Payment Required** naming the balance.

`source: "pixelscope"` unlocks up to 10 images per side and is the precondition for the Pixel Verified badge — but it grants nothing on its own. The caller's plan decides, and a Free plan gets 403.

Standard scans: max 1 image per side (front + back — the Quick Import shape). PixelScope: up to 10 per side. `slotIndex` is 0–9 within each side.
Returns the candidate matches to choose from at the confirmation step.
Captures the first result into `cardId` for the confirm and price requests.

Run **Get analysis** first to see the candidate matches, then confirm one.

Picking a card other than the suggested best match sets `wasCorrected` — retained as training signal.

Candidate `matchScore` is Scrydex's raw scale (~0.7–1.3+, unbounded). Rank with it; it is **not** a percentage.

exec: console.warn('400 here usually means step 3 (confirm) has not run yet.');

request.description:
Returns **400** if the analysis has no `confirmedCard`.

Re-running this on an already-graded analysis returns the existing report rather than re-invoking the model.

Results are cached in Redis under `grading:{modelVersion}:{imageSetHash}` with no TTL — the same image set always replays the original grade. `pixelVerified` is never cached and is recomputed per analysis.

item.name: Analysis Report
item.description:
Page: /user-dashboard/analysis-report

Recent inspection card + recent reports list. "Add card" button on the report → Add to collection (scanned).

request.description: Carries `grade` (0-10), `gradeLabel`, four sub-scores, `confidence` (0-100), `pixelVerified`, and `modelVersion`.
Returns application/pdf bytes (a download, not JSON). Watermarked when the report owner is on a plan with watermarkReports (Free by default); paid plans get a clean PDF. Rendered fresh per download.

Send `report` for a scanned card — the card is read from the report, so a client cannot attach someone else's grade to a card.

`currentPrice` is deliberately not accepted; price is system-owned.

item.name: My Collection
item.description:
Page: /user-dashboard/my-collection

Stats row → Summary. Card grid → List collection. Add-card modal (manual entry) → Search catalogue + Add manual. Favourite toggle → Update item.

request.description: `averageGrade` covers graded entries only and is `null` when nothing is graded — not zero.
Captures the first result into `cardId` for the confirm and price requests.
Manual entries have no AI grade. `externalGrade` records a third-party grade and is never conflated with ours.
Removes the entry only. The grading report and its images are retained permanently.

item.name: Price Tracker
item.description:
Page: /user-dashboard/price-tracker

**Collector plan and above** — Free gets 403 on all three.

Market stat cards → Portfolio summary. The table's per-row 30d sparklines → Batch history (ONE call for the whole visible page, not one per row). Row detail → Card price history.

request.description: Change percentages are value-weighted, not a plain mean — a large move on a high-value card outweighs the same move on a common.

One request for a whole table of sparklines instead of one per row.

Points are bucketed — daily for 7d/30d, monthly for 1y, raw for 24h — and each bucket carries its **closing** price. Response is a map keyed by card id; a card with no history yet comes back as `[]`.

item.name: Slab Generator
item.description:
Page: /user-dashboard/slab-generator

Style picker → List styles. Generate → Create slab label. Regenerate button → Regenerate background. Preview pane → Preview PNG. PNG/PDF download → the export URLs on Get label.

Backgrounds are generated by OpenAI gpt-image-1 (client-approved 2026-07-19) on the same API key as grading — verified live. Each generate/regenerate is a billed image (~$0.06 at medium quality).

exec: console.warn('503 means OPENAI_API_KEY is not set on the server.');

request.description:
Styles: cosmic, inferno, aurora, vintage.

Geometry is deliberately not accepted in the body — dimensions are server-owned so a client cannot resize the card window.

Background comes from gpt-image-1 and is stored permanently in Cloudinary. A 503 here means OPENAI_API_KEY is missing from the server env.
Includes `exportPngUrl` and `exportPdfUrl`.
Replaces only the AI background and bumps `version`. The card image and label text are composited server-side and never move.
Returns `image/png` bytes, not JSON. Postman renders it in the preview pane.

item.name: Subscription
item.description:
Page: /user-dashboard/subscription

Plan cards → List plans. Current plan banner + renewal date → My subscription. Upgrade button → Create checkout (open checkoutUrl in browser). Billing history → My transactions.

Yearly charges effective-monthly ×12 up front, but credits still refresh monthly.

request.description:
Free, Collector, Pro, Enterprise. Always exactly four — there is no create or delete route.

Captures a paid plan's id into `planId` for the checkout request.
Plan, renewal date, and credit position in one call.

Returns `{ checkoutUrl, sessionId }` — open `checkoutUrl` in a browser to complete payment.

`interval` is `monthly` or `yearly`. The **Free** plan is rejected with 400: it is the implicit default for any account without a paid subscription.

A subscription is only ever activated by a verified Stripe webhook, never by this call.
Cancels at period end, not immediately — the user keeps access through the period they paid for.

Profile → Get + Update. Change password / Security → Change password (or Set password for Google-born accounts). Data & privacy → Delete my account (soft delete; images and reports are retained as training data).

item.name: 02 · Admin Dashboard
item.description: Everything under /admin. **Log in as admin or super_admin first** — a `user` token gets 403 on every request here.

item.name: Dashboard Home
item.description:
Page: /admin

Stat cards row → Admin overview (totalUsers, subscribedUsers, newSubscribers, totalEarnings + mrr). Recent users table → List users.

`delta` is null when last month was zero — render no chip. `subscribedUsers.delta` undercounts churn (documented in the service).

request.description:
`totalUsers`, `subscribedUsers`, `newSubscribers`, `totalEarnings`, `mrr`.

`totalEarnings.value` is lifetime revenue; its delta compares this month against last.

**`subscribedUsers.delta` is approximate** — subscriptions store current status, not history, so churn is invisible to it.

item.name: Users
item.description:
Pages: /admin/users and /admin/users/[userId]

Table → List users (searchTerm matches name/email). Block modal → Block user (status + blockReason; unblock = status active). Details page plan/credit panel → User ledger.

⚠️ The table's Country and State columns have no backing field on the user model — nothing to wire yet.

request.description: Unblock by sending `{ "status": "active" }`.

Non-zero integer; negative values deduct.

This is one of only three ways credits enter a wallet — the others are a scheduled grant and a refund. There is deliberately no user-facing grant route.

item.name: Subscribed Users
item.description:
Page: /admin/subscribed-users

Driven from subscriptions, not accounts — defaults to active + past-due.

request.description: Defaults to active plus past-due. Driven from subscriptions rather than accounts, since "subscribed" is not a field on a user.

item.name: Earnings
item.description:
Page: /admin/earnings

Stat cards → Earnings (totals) + Subscription stats (MRR, active subs). Chart → Revenue by month. Transactions table → All transactions.

request.description: `grossRevenue`, `subscriptionRevenue`, `slabOrderRevenue`, counts, and refunds.

`activeSubscriptions`, `mrr`, `newThisMonth`, `newLastMonth`.

MRR takes `priceYearly` verbatim for yearly subscribers because that field is already the effective monthly rate. Past-due counts toward neither figure.

item.name: Subscription Plans
item.description:
Page: /admin/subscription-plan

Edit-only: the four tiers are fixed, `name` is immutable, there is no create or delete. `creditAmount: null` = unlimited (Enterprise). Mirror any change into pixel-grade-ai/src/config/plans.ts.

request.description:
Edit only. **`name` cannot be changed** and there is no create or delete route — the four tiers are fixed.

`creditAmount: null` means unlimited (Enterprise).

`priceYearly` is the **effective monthly** rate; Stripe charges it ×12 up front. Credits still refresh monthly regardless.

item.description:

`open` | `answered` | `resolved` | `closed`.

item.name: 03 · Reference & System
item.description: Not tied to a screen.

request.description: Probes Mongo and Redis. Returns **503 when a dependency is down** — that is the endpoint working correctly, not the endpoint failing.
No DB or Redis dependency — answers as long as the process is up.

**Cannot be exercised from Postman.** Authenticity comes from an HMAC over the exact raw bytes Stripe sent, so a hand-made request will always fail signature verification.

Use the Stripe CLI instead:

```
stripe listen --forward-to localhost:5000/webhook/stripe
stripe trigger checkout.session.completed
```

Handled events: `checkout.session.completed`, `invoice.payment_succeeded`, `invoice.payment_failed`, `customer.subscription.deleted`.
